title: Unattended server
summary: A persistent install serves the LAN unattended: SSH by keys only, binary-safe transfers, supervised services with logs, synchronized time, clean reboots, watchdog recovery, the resting state and remote upgrades with automatic rollback.

categories.title: Keys-only SSH: per-install host keys, per-account authorized keys, no password or telnet

cases.title: SSH identification arrives on port 22 before the client sends anything
OpenSSH keyscan matches the Ed25519 fingerprint in this boot's protected service log
Strict host-key checking permits the operator key and a non-root identity
OpenSSH authenticates and executes with aes256-gcm forced in both directions
OpenSSH authenticates and executes with aes128-ctr forced in both directions
An authorized Ed25519 user key authenticates and executes
OpenSSH password-only login and a real bssh password request are refused, with serial evidence
An unauthorized Ed25519 key is refused by publickey authentication
The authorized operator key cannot log in as root
Neither the standard nor the former development telnet port has a listener
An interactive SSH PTY supports foreground jobs, terminal signals and owned slave
SSH exec runs through bsh -c and returns the command exit status
SSH exec delivers piped input byte for byte and closes stdin on channel EOF
Quoted sh -c scripts retain spaces, quotes and backslashes through bsh

categories.title: Binary-safe exec stdin and verified uploads over SSH
Service supervision: dependencies, restart with backoff, crash-loop reporting, graceful stop

cases.title: svc reports bsshd, blogd, the time client and the six gettys from /etc/breenix/services, with their state under /run
bsshd starts once the random pool is ready, and the gettys start on the first pass without waiting for it
The time client starts only once the network is up
After kill -9 of bsshd, OpenSSH reconnects with strict host-key checking within the restart window
After the restart the operator key logs in to bsh again
A service that keeps failing quickly restarts after doubling delays of 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds
svc stop ends a service with SIGTERM, kills one that ignores it at its stop timeout, and neither restarts
A service runs as the account its entry names, and only that account or root may control it
Five quick failures are reported as a crash loop on the console and in svc, and the next start follows 60 seconds later

categories.title: Per-service and kernel logs with boot IDs and size-bounded rotation

cases.title: Every table service has a protected size-bounded log headed with this boot ID
A supervised service records stdout and stderr in its own file
A service log rotates at its size bound and retains complete records
An oversized line is counted as lost and the following line is retained
blogd records new kernel output and reports ring overruns
The previous persistent boot service log survives reboot with its original boot ID and bytes

categories.title: SNTP synchronization, slewing after the first step, RTC kept in UTC

cases.title: The supervised time client synchronizes from site or DHCP servers after network-up
The synchronized machine clock agrees with the boot host UTC within one second
The running client polls again after one hour without restarting
Invalid, unsynchronized, mismatched, stale and excessive-offset SNTP replies cannot change the clock
A negative correction after first synchronization slews at bounded rate without stepping backwards
After synchronization and reboot the hardware RTC agrees with the boot host UTC within one second

categories.title: Reboot and power-off after sync and a read-only remount; a panic reboots
A hang is reset by the watchdog back into the persistent install
Test boots preempt the persistent install and the machine returns to it
Remote upgrades verified over SSH and rolled back automatically

cases.title: A good upgrade passes strict operator SSH and service verification within 600 seconds of power-on, preserving host key and root and home sentinels
A deliberately broken upgrade fails verification and automatically boots the previous paired generation, passing the same probe within another 600 seconds with unchanged machine data
Installer ENOSPC, I/O and interrupted-publication recovery retain the selected generation and byte-exact rollback
Reclamation uses recovered on-disk slot userlands and preserves current, previous, in-flight and shared data across failures and rollback
